CONCLUSION: C1/C2/C5 realness is untouched by this correction and stands. C3's zero cannot currently be distinguished from an INSTRUMENT/TEST-DESIGN defect (the reachability gate never demonstrated it could register a flip on ANY arm, including one where an in-principle flip should have been possible) versus a genuine F-dominance negative result. Both readings remain open pending a corrected instrument.

targets.recommended_evidence_quality_note: V3-EXQ-964a (2026-09-11, diagnostic, supersedes V3-EXQ-964) does NOT bear on MECH-482's own claim hypothesis. This run arms the epistemic-deficit accumulator on BOTH arms and manipulates only the readiness geometry (match-radius mode, center-update, readout-mode, cross-episode persistence, target-frame). C1 (max_n_targets>=2) and C2 (cross-candidate readout range>0) both PASS non-arithmetically on all 3 seeds (max_n_targets 14-16, max_lp_dev_range 4.4e-3 to 7.3e-3), and C5 independently confirms the pre-readiness arm reproduces the OLD n_targets==1 collapse as a measured negative control -- i.e. the multitarget-readiness substrate build (sd_epistemic_deficit_multitarget_readiness) is now VALIDATED: the accumulator genuinely differentiates across candidates, closing exactly the gap V3-EXQ-964's autopsy named. However C3 (yoked downstream divergence) still measured 0/540 across all seeds. An independent adversarial red-team pass (Step 7c, CONTESTED, confirmed by this session's own recompute) found that the driver's own magnitude-reachability instrument -- the thing meant to establish this zero was a real measurement rather than an arithmetic artifact like V3-EXQ-964's -- is itself uninformative: its reachable-tick counts (n_margin_reads, n_flip_reachable_ticks, n_zero_margin_ticks, min_argmax_margin) are BYTE-IDENTICAL between ARM_READINESS and the structurally-inert ARM_PREREADINESS control at every seed, and at least 3 of the 10 counted 'ties' carry a strictly NEGATIVE margin (meaning arbitration had already overridden the score-based choice, or the margin measures a pre-arbitration stale snapshot) rather than a genuine near-tie. So this run does NOT establish that a flip was ever reachable at all, on either arm -- the predecessor autopsy's recommended positive control (inject a synthetic deficit large enough to force a flip) was never added, and its absence is now shown to matter. epistemic_category stays substrate_conditional and status stays candidate; retest is owed with a corrected reachability instrument and/or a positive-control arm, not simply a higher weight, before either a supports or weakens verdict on MECH-482 is warranted.

re_derive_brake.note: PRODUCER RELEASE (explicit). Under the mechanical R1-R3 counting recipe this target's non_contributory direction + substrate_conditional category DOES reach the literal count of 2 for MECH-482 (the sole prior hit being V3-EXQ-964). This autopsy declines to treat that as a ceiling and does NOT fire the brake. Reasoning updated after the Step 7c red-team pass (CONTESTED, confirmed by this session's own recompute): C1/C2/C5 remain a REAL, non-arithmetic pass -- the multitarget-readiness substrate build is validated -- independent of the red-team finding. The C3 zero, however, is now understood NOT as a config-only shortfall (raise the weight) but as UNRESOLVED pending a corrected reachability instrument: the magnitude-reachability gate that would certify this as a real (rather than arithmetic-artifact) test of C3 is itself shown to be uninformative (byte-identical reachable-tick counts on the structurally-inert control arm; several counted 'ties' are strictly negative margins). Under R3, an instrument/test-design reading is ALSO a non-counting category (clause 2), so the brake stays un-fired either way this is read -- but the correct next step is a corrected instrument and/or positive-control arm, not simply a higher weight. If a corrected-instrument re-queue STILL reads non_contributory with a demonstrably-working reachability gate (i.e. one that discriminates the two arms), that would be the first genuine substrate_ceiling-equivalent hit for MECH-482, and the brake should very likely fire on the occurrence AFTER that -- this release is not open-ended.

learning_extracted: A substrate-readiness build can be genuinely validated (C1/C2 real, non-arithmetic, independently confirmed by a measured collapse control) while the claim it was built to test STILL receives zero support -- these are two separable facts and both must be recorded. Treating a validated readiness build as automatically clearing the way for a claim verdict would be premature; the downstream arbitration/weighting layer is a distinct, separately-testable gate.

RED-TEAM FINDING (confirmed): a reachability instrument that passes ITS OWN threshold is not evidence of reachability unless it is shown to DISCRIMINATE a positive case from a case where reachability is impossible by construction. Here the instrument (n_flip_reachable_ticks via fmargin<=0.0) returned BYTE-IDENTICAL counts on ARM_READINESS and on ARM_PREREADINESS -- an arm the driver's own per_arm_gate note declares structurally incapable of any argmax flip 'at ANY magnitude' -- which proves the instrument was measuring an arm-invariant (F-only, pre-perturbation) quantity, not the perturbation under test. A future instrument in this family needs a demonstrated positive control (a case where a flip IS produced) before its 'reachable' count can be trusted at all.

The predecessor autopsy (V3-EXQ-964) named the correct fix for exactly this situation -- a positive control / verify-lift arm -- and this driver declined it with a stated but unadjudicated rationale ('the margin instrumentation ... MEASURES reachability per tick instead of manufacturing it'). The declination was never checked against the instrument's own behaviour on the negative-control arm. A driver that declines a predecessor's recommended remedy should say what would falsify the substitute, not merely assert it is honest.

A weight-raise recommendation sized off a single run's single best tick (max_pert_over_margin) is fragile: the driver's OWN docstring records a 22x run-to-run swing in the underlying lp_dev_range statistic at fixed seed/config, and a separate smoke-based estimate of ~1.7e3x for parity -- two to three orders of magnitude apart from a naive 4-5x extrapolation off this run's best tick. Do not size a configuration fix off one run's extremum without checking it against the driver's own stated variability.

F-dominance at the committed-selection layer (max_pert_over_margin capping at 0.233 despite genuine, real differentiation upstream) resembles the same class of washout previously documented for structurally unrelated mechanisms (V3-EXQ-569g/684/700/709/710, the 'single-arena F-dominated selector' pattern that eventually motivated the segregated-loop substrate, v4_loop_segregation / ARC-110). This autopsy does not claim MECH-482 has hit that same architectural ceiling -- the reachability instrument itself is not yet trustworthy, so F-dominance is not yet established either -- but flags the structural resemblance for governance's cross-claim pattern-tracking, should a corrected-instrument retest also wash out.
